prompt: Review and harden a media-import service. A user can upload a ZIP archive or provide an HTTPS source URL, choose an output name, and supply converter options. The service fetches remote input, extracts the archive, writes files into a job directory, invokes a native converter, and stores generated output plus logs. Build a source-to-sink map and concrete application-security requirements for URL fetching, redirect/resolution behavior, archive paths and resource limits, output-path canonicalization, subprocess argument handling, parser limits, partial output cleanup, and safe errors/logging. Preserve authorization as a separate concern: assume the caller is already entitled to create the job. Resource ceilings must be explicit: when the existing product does not provide a numeric policy, choose and label conservative provisional limits instead of leaving body/output/time/memory/process/log bounds qualitative. Define reproducible negative cases, including a full bearer Authorization header and terminal controls in diagnostic text, and fail-closed behavior, but leave final black-box proof of the finished implementation to security-verification.

requirements: media-import service with remote URL, archive, output-name, and converter-option inputs
FetchHop array modeling URL/resolved-IP pairs; no HTTP transport or connected-peer observation is supplied
archive metadata validator and path helper with real temporary roots; no ZIP parser/extractor is supplied
converter invocation descriptor with fixed executable and --quality low|medium|high contract; no converter process or durable job pipeline is supplied
implement and test supplied helpers; record absent transport/parser/process/persistence boundaries as integration blockers rather than claiming runtime proof

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result traces each attacker-controlled URL/archive/path/option value through decoding/normalization to outbound-request, filesystem, archive-parser, subprocess, persistence, and log/error sinks with a concrete invariant before each privileged sink.

Tests use existing temporary roots: permit a nested relative target and reject absolute, parent-traversal, normalized escape, and escaping symlink/reparse targets. Apply containment to both archive and output paths, including existing leaf links and new-target ancestors. Specify race-safe creation and no outside-root writes; identify any missing write/extract integration as unverified.

Declare numeric ceilings with units and enforcement points for redirects, archive entries/expanded bytes/per-entry bytes/depth, body/output bytes, processing time, converter memory/process count, and diagnostic bytes. Preserve supplied ceilings; label missing-policy defaults as provisional. Exercise permitted values, exact boundaries, overflow, and invalid/non-finite metadata. Mark absent parser/process limit enforcement as unverified rather than treating constants or prose as proof.

Use a fixed executable and shell-free structured argv, preserve supported --quality low|medium|high options and valid punctuation, and test rejected unsupported options plus leading-option operands. Explain option/operand separation using the converter's documented parser; -- is useful only where supported. A descriptor containing safe-looking strings is not proof of the converter's actual effects; record missing executable/parser evidence as a blocker.

Permit a valid public HTTPS control; reject malformed/non-HTTPS/userinfo URLs, private/loopback/link-local and non-public destinations, redirect-to-private targets, and excessive hops under the fixture's public-network policy. Test IPv4/IPv6 and mapped forms. Require the actual connection, retries, and redirects to use vetted destinations with TLS hostname checks and safe cross-origin header handling. A resolvedIp field alone does not prove connected-peer/DNS-rebinding enforcement; record absent transport evidence as a blocker.

Retain useful non-sensitive diagnostic context while removing a full Authorization: Bearer credential, access/refresh credentials and bare aliases across newlines/delimiters, and terminal controls; test long messages against the declared byte cap. Specify and, where implemented, exercise failure after partial staging, no outside-root or committed partial output, deterministic cleanup/quarantine, and a later valid retry. Record missing persistence/cleanup execution as unverified.

evidence: executable helper regressions with permitted controls and rejected inputs
negative-case matrix separating observed results from integration blockers

requiredEvidence: negative and cleanup/failure cases with unverified integration boundaries labeled
